correctness.rationale: The final-time burning arcs have lengths 2k-1,2k-3,...,1 summing to k^2. A square-order cover forces disjoint tilings; the single-unit deficit forces exactly one duplicate point. Removing the radius-zero singleton partitions all schedules into (A) disjoint positive-radius arcs plus endpoint singleton, or (B) one adjacent overlap among positive arcs and one uncovered singleton position. Cyclic orders of positive arc centers are conserved by valid single-coordinate exchanges, while deficit transport and unit translations connect every schedule of fixed order. Enumerating the two types and their moves gives each count, component size and degree histogram. Independent brute-force generation from distance and cover definitions confirms all k=2,3,4 both orders, including complete exchange graphs. No finite extrapolation is needed for all k.

value.rationale: One-site relaxation of the maximum coverage capacity k^2 is a natural sharp extremal boundary. It creates local mobility from fully isolated square-order solutions while leaving factorially many components; full degree, edge and component-size formulas characterize a nontrivial reconfiguration state space on every cycle length in the two natural regimes.

final_claim: For proper time-labeled optimal k-burning schedules on C_N, k>=2: at N=k^2, exactly k^2(k-1)! isolated schedules; at N=k^2-1, exactly Nk! schedules, (k-2)! coordinate-exchange components of size Nk(k-1), N(3k-4)(k-1)! edges, with degree classes 2 and 2k-2 as specified.
limitations: Alternative definitions permitting already burned ignitions, rotational quotient or swapping time labels have different reconfiguration graphs; the theorem intentionally excludes them.
